theory.name: r5-account
theory.statement: On MATH-500 at AI2's setting (T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample each), the 65 problems that Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math gets right and the cued Olmo 3 base gets wrong break down into four mechanisms and a small remainder. (1) Budget: about 0.25 are problems where the cued base ran to the 16,384-token cap without a loop. These are long problems on which the base keeps going and never commits, while RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. (2) Answer statement: about 0.15 are problems where the base's failure was in stating the answer: a right value in a rejected or garbled final line, or a reached gold that it then overwrote. (3) Reliability: about 0.51 are problems the base solves in at least one of four other independent samples. The miss here is a sample-specific slip or misread on a problem the base can do, and RL removes it by concentrating on paths the base already samples. This is the largest part and the one still open. (4) Capability: about 0.07 are problems the base never solves in four further samples while RL solves at least two of four. Here RL uses a plan the base does not sample. (Unassigned) About 0.02 are problems where RL's single right answer was itself a lucky draw: RL is right in at most one of four other samples.
theory.gap: Cells: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, T1 = base Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token opening cue and T2 = Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the plain prompt, both MATH-500 (500 problems), T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384 new tokens, 1 sample, grader v3 (fields t1_right, t2_right). A gap problem is a row with t2_right true and t1_right false (cell rl_only). Cap hits count as wrong through their stored t1_right/t2_right, and a row with t1_right or t2_right null or missing is not a gap problem. Expected size is 65 problems (result-5e17a6). The rules also read the independent 4-sample rows of the same two models at the same setting: D = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and E = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl, attempt == 0, samples 0-3. kB and kR are the numbers of those rows with score_v3 == 1. Cap-hit rows, null score_v3 and missing samples count as wrong, and a duplicated (problem_index, sample) uses its first row in file order.

parts.name: budget
parts.mechanism: The cued base keeps writing past the 16,384-token budget without committing on long problems (no rule-A loop at T 1.0), while RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. This revives the termination idea of r1-across-2 and r1-surprises-1, which were refuted on weight-dose answer counts (theta 1.5 word salad) and on a hard328 pass@4 count, not on which stored problems hit the cap, so their refuting tests do not apply to this per-problem rule.
parts.rule: per_problem.json row of the problem has t1_cap_hit == true.

parts.name: answer-statement
parts.mechanism: The base reaches the right value but fails at stating it: a final line that v3 rejects or that is garbled, or a gold value overwritten by a later answer marker (the untested r4-m11/r4-m12 mechanisms, not refuted). RL boxes once and stops.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and the per_problem.json field failure_type, lower-cased, contains at least one of the substrings 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected', 'changed'. A null or missing failure_type is not taken.

parts.name: reliability
parts.mechanism: The base can solve the problem, and the T1 miss is a sample-specific slip or misread. RL sharpens the base's own distribution onto paths it already samples. This revives the slip-removal readings of r2-revise-2 and r3-surprises-1. Their refuting tests were a hard328 vote@4 count and a vote tie-break count, which make claims about vote procedures, not about whether the base solves a gap problem in independent samples, so they do not apply here.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and kB >= 1 (at least one of the 4 attempt-0 base_cue rows in D with score_v3 == 1).

parts.name: capability
parts.mechanism: RL uses a plan the base does not sample on this problem: the base fails all four independent samples, while RL solves the problem repeatedly.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and kB == 0 and kR >= 2 (at least two of the 4 attempt-0 RL rows in E with score_v3 == 1).

theory.scope: Covers the 65 RL-only problems of the stored MATH-500 T1/T2 pair at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, grader v3, one sample per model. It does not cover the 12 base-only problems (the gap counted here is gross, not net), T 0.6 cells (where loops dominate), the hard328 set, the Code pair or 3.0 checkpoints. Part 2 rests on one reader's hand label (failure_type). Parts 3-4 classify with 4 further samples per model, so a problem with a base rate near 0.1 can fall into capability by chance.

imports.finding: RLVR raises pass@1 by concentrating on paths the base model already samples. Per-problem MATH-500 coverage at 128 samples is almost the same for both models.
imports.how: Grounds the reliability part: on most gap problems the base's own samples already contain the right path, so RL's gain there is concentration, not new reach.

imports.finding: Rule-based math verifiers miss correctly formatted variants (average recall 86 %).
imports.how: Grounds the answer-statement part: some base gap misses are right values in forms the rule-based v3 rejects.

imports.finding: In Olmo 3, RL-Zero-Math multiplies an existing 'wait' marker. At T 0.6 RL hits the length limit more often than the base.
imports.how: Places the budget part in termination policy rather than skill: RL changes when the model keeps checking and when it stops.

Base-0/4 problems fail by wrong plan, which matches the separate, small capability part.

conflicts.how: Label-free extraction rules repair only 0.5 points, which is less than a 0.15 answer-statement share suggests. Either the hand label overstates format failures, or many of them are forms (garbled lines, overwritten gold) that no extraction rule can repair.

theory.rival: The strongest rival is a pure sampling-noise budget: every gap problem is a draw from the base's per-problem success rate, so cap hits and answer-statement misses are just ways a sample fails and are not separate mechanisms. Under it, the cap-hit gap problems behave like the rest: the random matched-norm cell (a fresh base sample) solves them at about the overall 40/65 = 0.62 rate, and their other base samples cap no more often than base samples in general. This account instead predicts that the random cell solves only about 0.35 of the budget problems and that about 0.75 of them have at least one other cap hit in D. The random-cell solve rate on the budget part is the number that separates the two (0.35 here against about 0.6 under the rival).

theory.name: r6-account
theory.statement: The problems that an RL-side model gets right and the cued Olmo 3 base gets wrong split into five mechanisms, applied in this order. (1) Loop: the base runs to the 16,384-token cap inside a self-reinforcing repeat (rule A). This is a sampler artifact of truncated, low-temperature decoding (T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). It is absent at T 1.0, and the base can usually do these problems at T 1.0. (2) Budget: the base hits the cap without a loop. These are long problems on which it never commits, while RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. (3) Answer statement: the base finishes but writes no answer line, or writes the gold value in a box or 'Answer:' line and then ends on another value. (4) Reliability: the base solves the problem in at least one independent stored base sample, so the miss is a sample-specific slip that RL removes by concentrating on paths the base already samples. (5) Capability: no independent base sample solves it. On the known cell (MATH-500, T 1.0, cued base against Olmo-3.1 RL) the shares are 0 / 0.25 / 0.15 / 0.54 / 0.06. I predict how the shares move in three other cells. Against the half-dose weight blend theta0.5 at T 1.0, budget falls to about 0.17 and reliability rises to about 0.70, because theta0.5 keeps almost the base's cap rate but already has the sharpening. On hard328 against Code-RL at T 1.0, the shares are loop 0.02, budget 0.25, answer 0.08, reliability 0.34 and capability 0.31: capability grows on the harder set, where the base's independent evidence is weaker. On MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 against RL step 400 (grader v1), loop takes about 0.50, with budget 0.13, answer 0.17 (v1 misses on the base's 'Answer:' lines), reliability 0.15 and capability 0.05. The largest part still open at T 1.0 is reliability, and the base-only route to it is more independent votes, weighted toward high-precision finished answers.

parts.name: loop
parts.mechanism: Under truncated low-temperature sampling (top-p 0.95 at T 0.6) the base's repeat probabilities lock and it loops to the cap on problems it can otherwise finish. RL-side samples escape the loop, and at T 1.0 the part is empty.
parts.rule: The base row is a cap hit (cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length') and rule A fires on its text. Rule A: for every character position p that is 0 or directly follows a newline and has at least 8,000 characters to the end, w = text[p:p+8000]; it fires if any len(zlib.compress(w.encode('utf-8')))/len(w.encode('utf-8')) < 0.10 (Python zlib, default level). Shorter or missing text does not fire.

parts.name: budget
parts.mechanism: The base keeps writing past the token budget without committing on long problems, while the RL side, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. This revives the termination idea of r1-across-2 and r1-surprises-1, which were refuted on weight-dose answer counts and a hard328 pass@4 count, not on which stored problems hit the cap. Those tests do not apply to this per-problem rule.
parts.rule: Not taken by loop, and the base row is a cap hit (cap_hit true, or missing and finish_reason == 'length').

parts.name: answer-statement
parts.mechanism: The base fails in stating the answer: it writes no answer line, or it writes the gold value and then ends on another value (the untested r4-m11 mechanism). RL boxes once and stops.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier. With N(s) = s with all whitespace, '$', '*' and '#' deleted, '\left' and '\right' deleted, and '\dfrac'/'\tfrac' replaced by '\frac', and g = N(gold): taken if no N(line) of the base text contains '\boxed{' and none starts with 'Answer:', or some N(line) contains '\boxed{'+g+'}', or some N(line) equals 'Answer:'+g or 'Answer:'+g+'.'. Missing text is taken.

parts.name: reliability
parts.mechanism: The base can solve the problem, and the miss is a sample-specific slip that RL removes by sharpening onto paths the base already samples. This revives r2-revise-2 and r3-surprises-1, whose refuting tests were hard328 vote@4 and tie-break counts, claims about vote procedures rather than about whether independent base samples solve a gap problem.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier, and kB >= 1, where kB = the number of the cell's independent base evidence rows E for this problem that are right.

parts.name: capability
parts.mechanism: The RL side uses a plan the base does not sample: no independent stored base sample solves the problem.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier, E holds at least one row, and kB == 0.

theory.scope: The account covers gross gap problems (RL side right, base wrong; base-only problems are not counted) in four cells. They span both problem sets (MATH-500 and hard328), both sampling settings (T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 and T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and four model pairs (final RL, theta0.5 blend, Code-RL 3.1, RL step 400). Left out: the hard328 cued-base-vs-RL T 1.0 cell, because board item result-5de032 already gives its cap/finished budget (16/33 of 49); it is used as an anchor, not predicted. Also left out: MATH-500 T 0.6 cued base vs RL step 2,800, because knowledge-9e4147 gives a cap-hit budget for it (85 of 123). hard328 has no readable independent cued-T 1.0 base samples: the 4-sample rows of result-1dedfe are on sameraslan's Volume, which is not in the inventory. conflicts.quote: a=0.25 is +6.2 pts over base cue
conflicts.how: A flat dose curve after a = 0.25 sits uneasily with this account's claim that the budget part needs a dose-dependent commit policy that theta0.5 still lacks.

theory.rival: The strongest rival is a single-difficulty budget. Every gap problem is a draw at the base's per-problem success rate, and loop, budget and reliability are only ways a hard problem fails, not separate mechanisms. Under it, a model that fixes more gap problems fixes all parts in proportion, and the base's T 0.6 loop problems are as hard for the base at T 1.0 as any long problem (a T 1.0 solve rate of about 0.35, its rate on the longest quartile of base failures). This account predicts that theta0.5's fix rate on reliability-part problems exceeds its fix rate on budget-part problems by about 0.30 (rival: about 0). It also predicts that the base's T 1.0 sample solves about 0.52 of its T 0.6 rule-A loop problems (rival: about 0.35). The theta0.5 reliability-minus-budget fix-rate difference is the number that separates the two.
